summary: Checked 8 claims against LinkedIn's official docs on Microsoft Learn. Numbers and policies were accurate; one step overstated its evidence. The 'Easy' rating holds only for Composio's default self-serve scopes, which the guide states.

corrections.claim: Self-serve access tokens last 60 days; refresh tokens (365 days, TTL not reset on use) are only for approved MDP partners
corrections.finding: Confirmed verbatim in 'Refresh Tokens with OAuth 2.0'.
Confirmed in the Share on LinkedIn throttle table.

corrections.claim: Community Management Development tier: 500 calls/app/day, 100/member/day, no BATCH_GET, no webhooks, 12 months to build
A rejected Community Management application cannot re-apply with the same app
corrections.finding: Confirmed: 'create a new app, and submit a new Development tier access request form.'

corrections.claim: Step 'Apply for Community Management API on a dedicated app' labeled Documented
corrections.finding: Its two key specifics (API must be the only product on the app; 21-day survey window) are not on the official App Review page. Relabeled Reported and reworded.

corrections.claim: Community Management API must be alone on its app
corrections.finding: Plausible and widely reported, but not stated in official docs fetched. Only a real Products-tab attempt would confirm.

corrections.claim: Unverified app (Page admin hasn't approved) can't use self-serve products
corrections.finding: Not resolvable from docs; needs a logged-in attempt. Left in uncertainties.
